subject: math

objective.text: Equal parts of the same shape can look different. They still take up the same space.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Recognize that equal parts of an identical rectangle can have different shapes.

explanations.title: Many ways to make equal parts
explanations.text: You can cut a square into halves in different ways. The halves can be rectangles or triangles.

explanations.title: Different shape, same space
explanations.text: A triangle half and a rectangle half of the same square cover the same amount of space.

explanations.title: Move the parts, keep the whole
explanations.text: Move the halves to make a new shape. The parts are still halves. The whole did not change.

examples.title: Proving two halves are equal
examples.text: Cut the triangle half into 4 small triangles. They cover the rectangle half with no gaps. So the halves are equal.

questions.text: Tugu made 2 pizzas for himself and his 5 friends. Everyone gets an equal share. How should he cut each pizza?
A square is cut corner to corner into 2 triangles of the same size. Is it cut into halves?

misconceptions.description: Child thinks two parts cannot be equal because they are different shapes.
